Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance and Budgets (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos) and the General Treasury are statutory members of CNEDOGE's governing Board (Consejo de Administración) per Decree No. 24/2010. The Deputy Director of CNEDOGE is nominated by the Ministry of Finance. Budget oversight is formally embedded.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The cited source reproduces Decreto 24/2010 in detail: the Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos and the Tesorería General del Estado are listed as 'miembros natos' (statutory members) of CNEDOGE's Consejo de Administración alongside the Ministries of National Security, Foreign Affairs and Interior, and the Deputy Director is nominated by Hacienda — consistent with shared/partial rather than full or no oversight (CNEDOGE is organically attached to the Ministry of National Security, whose head nominates the Director General). Corroborated against the decree's listing on the official Ministry of Finance website. Value Code 2 (Partial oversight) confirmed, unchanged.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: CNEDOGE operates an internal electronic database for document issuance (active since 2018). The SIREC (Sistema Informático del Registro Civil) pilot digital civil registry operates in Malabo since 2018 (UNICEF/Ministry of Justice). No centralized national database or government-wide system exists; no expansion to mainland funded yet.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed in substance, with a caveat. CNEDOGE's founding 2010 decree already mandates a biometric security system for document issuance, and a January 2025 government report confirms CNEDOGE runs a 'sala de base de datos de documentos oficiales' (though equipment is described as ageing following a December 2023 fire, with modernisation now planned). The World Bank's 2023/24 Digital Economy Diagnostic confirms the Malabo-only SIREC civil-registry pilot (2018) and states no centralised, government-wide digital identity system yet exists, recommending one be built — supporting 'Mix of paper and digital' rather than fully digital. The specific claim that CNEDOGE's own database dates precisely from 2018 is not independently corroborated (biometric capture appears to predate that, from the 2010 decree). Value Code 2 confirmed, unchanged.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: World Bank ID4D Global Dataset (2021/2022) estimates approximately 63% of adults hold the national ID card (DIP). This compares to 73% in Gabon and 82.8% in Cameroon. Birth registration coverage is 65.7% (2023 national household survey). Geographic disparities exist, with Bioko Island having higher coverage than the continental provinces.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a more precise source than originally cited. The World Bank ID4D Global Dataset 2021 (Volume 1, administrative-data annex) records 646,000 people registered in Equatorial Guinea's National ID System against an estimated 1,030,216 adult (15+) population, a 62.7% administrative coverage rate (2022 data), matching the 50-69% band. Note this is administrative registration data, not a Global Findex survey estimate — Equatorial Guinea appears to have been excluded from the 2021/22 and 2024 Global Findex survey rounds, so the original comment's framing as an 'ID4D Global Dataset' estimate is accurate but its likely derivation (Findex) is not; it is administrative. Value Code 3 (50-69%) confirmed, unchanged.
